nodes.notes: Operative machinery for both the Section 9.04(f) Affiliate Lender assignments and the Section 9.04(g) loan buybacks.

nodes.label: doc-a::I::ebitda
nodes.notes: Load-bearing for both financial covenants, the pricing grid, Material Subsidiary, and every EBITDA-scaled basket (15%/25% of Applicable EBITDA).

nodes.label: doc-a::I::ebitda-combined-cap
nodes.notes: A hard 20% cap shared across three add-back categories - a classic shared-cap relationship a pipeline could miss.

nodes.label: doc-a::I::ebitda-deemed-quarterly-amounts
nodes.notes: Hardwired historical EBITDA for LTM builds through Q4 2022 - directly changes early ratio results.

nodes.label: doc-a::I::erisa-and-canadian-pension-definitions
nodes.notes: Feed the 5.02(d) notice trigger ($5M) and the 7.01(l) Event of Default ($20M), and the 6.03(g) prohibition on Canadian defined benefit plans.

nodes.label: doc-a::I::indebtedness
nodes.notes: The earn-out carve-out (only counted once reflected as a balance-sheet liability and unpaid when due) is economically significant for acquisition-heavy borrowers.

nodes.label: doc-a::I::interest-coverage-ratio
nodes.notes: The annualization convention changes the covenant result for the first four test dates.

nodes.label: doc-a::I::loan-parties-us-canadian
nodes.notes: ENTITY-APPLICABILITY: the U.S./Canadian split is enforced throughout (2.01 final paragraph, 5.13(e)(i), 6.09(b), 10.01(b), 11.07(a)) - Canadian Loan Parties never guarantee or secure U.S. Secured Obligations.

nodes.label: doc-a::I::material-acquisition
nodes.notes: Sole gating trigger for the Total Net Leverage Ratio Adjustment (leverage covenant holiday) in Section 6.12(b).

nodes.label: doc-a::I::material-indebtedness
nodes.notes: Sets the cross-default (7.01(f)) and cross-acceleration (7.01(g)) threshold at $20M, and the Section 5.04 payment covenant scope.

nodes.label: doc-a::I::material-subsidiary
nodes.notes: Drives which subsidiaries must join as guarantors and pledge collateral under Section 5.13(a), and which can be released under 10.08(b).

nodes.label: doc-a::I::off-balance-sheet-liability
nodes.notes: Interacts with Permitted Supply Chain Financing, which is structured as a true sale to avoid this.

nodes.label: doc-a::I::ordinary-administrative-definitions
nodes.notes: Grouped by design: these are definitional-only with no independent operative effect beyond the sections that use them.

nodes.label: doc-a::I::paid-in-full
nodes.notes: Sets the endpoint of the Article V and VI covenant periods and the release triggers in 9.02(c) and 10.08(c).

nodes.label: doc-a::I::permitted-acquisition
nodes.notes: Clause (h)(ii) is a 0.25x inside-the-covenant cushion measured against the level INCLUDING any Total Net Leverage Ratio Adjustment; clause (k) is a hard $50M lifetime non-guarantor/non-collateral basket.

nodes.label: doc-a::I::permitted-encumbrances
nodes.notes: Incorporated by reference into Section 6.02(b) as a standing Lien exception and into the 3.15 priority representation.

nodes.label: doc-a::I::permitted-investments
nodes.notes: Feeds both Section 6.04(a) (permitted investments basket) and the Unrestricted Cash definition.

nodes.label: doc-a::I::permitted-supply-chain-financing
nodes.notes: Enables the 6.01(o) debt basket, the 6.02(o) Lien basket and the 6.05(j) Disposition basket - a three-way linked exception.

nodes.label: doc-a::I::prepayment-event
nodes.notes: Only 6.05(k) sales trigger the sweep - all other permitted Dispositions escape mandatory prepayment. Clause (b) is a non-permitted-debt sweep.

nodes.label: doc-a::I::required-lenders
nodes.notes: Voting-power definition; interacts with 2.20(c) (Defaulting Lender disenfranchisement) and 9.04(f)(iv) (Affiliate Lender voting sterilization, Debt Fund Affiliate 25% cap).

nodes.label: doc-a::I::restricted-and-unrestricted-subsidiary
nodes.notes: ENTITY SCOPE: substantially every covenant in Articles V and VI binds only Loan Parties and Restricted Subsidiaries; every ratio is computed for the Company and Restricted Subsidiaries only.

nodes.label: Entity scope @ 1.01
nodes.notes: ENTITY SCOPE: substantially every covenant in Articles V and VI binds only Loan Parties and Restricted Subsidiaries; every ratio is computed for the Company and Restricted Subsidiaries only.

nodes.label: doc-a::I::returns-not-otherwise-applied
nodes.notes: Both are anti-double-counting mechanics inside the Available Amount build.

nodes.label: doc-a::I::sanctions-definitions
nodes.notes: Gate the 3.20 representation, the 5.07/5.08(b) covenants and the 2.06(a) LC issuance limits.

nodes.label: doc-a::I::subordinated-indebtedness
nodes.notes: Gates Section 1.07 (senior designation), 6.08(b)(ii) (no payments prohibited by subordination terms) and 6.11(a) (no adverse amendments).

nodes.label: doc-a::I::total-indebtedness
nodes.notes: The (i)/(m) carve-outs materially reduce the leverage numerator - undrawn LCs and swap MTM are excluded.

nodes.label: doc-a::I::total-net-leverage-ratio
nodes.notes: Cash netting is capped at $25M and only Unrestricted Cash (control-agreement cash of Loan Parties) counts.

nodes.label: doc-a::I::unrestricted-cash
nodes.notes: Control-agreement condition means cash at non-Loan-Party subsidiaries never nets against leverage. Also used in the Permitted Acquisition $10,000,000 liquidity test.

nodes.label: doc-a::I::us-and-canadian-secured-obligations
nodes.notes: This one-way ring-fence is the single most distinctive structural feature of the collateral/guarantee package.

nodes.label: doc-a::II::2.01-canadian-ringfence
nodes.notes: ENTITY-APPLICABILITY: the operative statement of the one-way Canadian ring-fence, reinforced in 5.13(e)(i), 10.01(b) and 11.07(a).

nodes.label: doc-a::II::2.05-swingline-loans
nodes.notes: Swingline availability is discretionary, not committed - relevant to actual liquidity capacity.

nodes.label: doc-a::II::2.06-letters-of-credit
nodes.notes: The $25,000,000 LC sublimit sits inside the $200,000,000 Revolving Commitments - a nested capacity relationship.

nodes.label: doc-a::II::2.09-incremental-facility
nodes.notes: $200,000,000 total incremental capacity is a hard dollar cap (no ratio-based freebie); note there is NO MFN/most-favored-nation pricing protection - pricing may differ freely.

nodes.label: doc-a::II::2.11a-optional-prepayment
nodes.notes: No call protection or prepayment premium on any tranche.

nodes.label: doc-a::II::2.11b-revolver-overadvance-cure
nodes.notes: The 102% FX cushion is a real, easily-missed operational allowance.

nodes.label: doc-a::II::2.11c-mandatory-prepayment-events
nodes.notes: CRITICAL: no excess cash flow sweep exists in this agreement; the asset-sale sweep only reaches Section 6.05(k) sales and only above $10M per fiscal year.

nodes.label: doc-a::II::2.11e-prepayment-application
nodes.notes: The 'first four scheduled repayments then ratably' waterfall is a specific, non-standard application order.

nodes.label: doc-a::II::2.11g-declined-amounts
nodes.notes: Borrower Retained Prepayment Amounts flow directly into the Available Amount builder (clause (vii)) - a linkage between the prepayment mechanics and Article VI basket capacity.

nodes.label: doc-a::II::2.12-fees
nodes.notes: Note the unusual Swingline exclusion from the commitment-fee 'drawn' calculation.

nodes.label: doc-a::II::2.13-interest
nodes.notes: Default interest is elective and requires notice, not automatic - a meaningful distinction on default consequences.

nodes.label: doc-a::II::2.18-payments-waterfall
nodes.notes: Swap/Banking Services obligations share the fourth tier with principal only up to the amount most recently notified under 2.22 - otherwise they drop to the sixth tier.

nodes.label: doc-a::II::2.22-banking-services-swaps
nodes.notes: The notice requirement is what converts hedging/cash-management exposure into meaningfully secured claims at tier four of the waterfall.

nodes.label: doc-a::III::3.04-financial-condition-no-mac
nodes.notes: The 3.04(a) financials are the fallback reference set for every 'most recent financial statements' calculation before the first Section 5.01 delivery.

nodes.label: doc-a::III::3.10-erisa
nodes.notes: The 'no Canadian Defined Benefit Pension Plan' representation pairs with the Section 6.03(g) prohibition on incurring one.

nodes.label: doc-a::III::3.12-solvency
nodes.notes: Tested on a 'taken as a whole' basis for Loan Parties, not entity by entity - relevant to fraudulent-transfer analysis alongside Sections 10.10 and 10.11.

nodes.label: doc-a::III::3.14-capitalization-subsidiaries
nodes.notes: Schedule 3.14 is the Effective Date designation of Unrestricted Subsidiaries referenced in the 'Unrestricted Subsidiary' definition; the schedule itself is not reproduced in this document.

nodes.label: doc-a::III::3.19-no-burdensome-restrictions
nodes.notes: Ties the negative-pledge/dividend-blocker representation directly to the Section 6.10 exception list.

nodes.label: doc-a::III::chapeau
nodes.notes: ENTITY SCOPE: representations are given by every Loan Party but most are qualified to Loan Parties and Restricted Subsidiaries, excluding Unrestricted Subsidiaries.

nodes.label: Entity scope @ III
nodes.notes: ENTITY SCOPE: representations are given by every Loan Party but most are qualified to Loan Parties and Restricted Subsidiaries, excluding Unrestricted Subsidiaries.

nodes.label: doc-a::IV::4.01-outside-date
nodes.notes: A hard commitment-termination outside date, not merely a milestone.

nodes.label: doc-a::IV::4.01b-closing-date-acquisitions
nodes.notes: This is a limited-conditionality ('certain funds') construct: the acquisition-agreement representation standard is limited to those representations whose breach would permit the Company to decline to close.

nodes.label: doc-a::IV::4.01k-filings
nodes.notes: The flush proviso following 4.01(k) is a genuine limited-conditionality collateral carve-out, not boilerplate.

nodes.label: doc-a::IV::4.01n-legal-diligence
nodes.notes: A sole-discretion diligence condition is unusually broad for a limited-conditionality acquisition financing.

nodes.label: doc-a::IV::4.02-each-credit-event
nodes.notes: The discretionary protective-advance override in the final paragraph is a genuinely operative Agent right, not boilerplate.

nodes.label: doc-a::IX::9.02b-amendment-thresholds
nodes.notes: CRITICAL: financial covenant levels (and the defined terms feeding them - EBITDA, Total Net Leverage Ratio, etc.) can be amended by REQUIRED LENDERS only. Guarantee release and all-or-substantially-all Collateral release are sacred rights.

nodes.label: doc-a::IX::9.02c-collateral-release-authority
nodes.notes: The $500,000 annual discretionary release allowance and the certificate-reliance mechanic are the practical route by which collateral leaves the package.

nodes.label: doc-a::IX::9.02e-technical-amendments
nodes.notes: A two-party amendment right without Lender consent - relevant to determining which version of a provision is operative.

nodes.label: doc-a::IX::9.04b-assignments
nodes.notes: The 25%-during-default concentration limit and the Disqualified Institution regime are real transfer restrictions with economic effect on who can hold the debt in a workout.

nodes.label: doc-a::IX::9.04f-affiliate-lenders
nodes.notes: CRITICAL: a 20% sponsor-affiliate holding cap and a 25% Debt Fund Affiliate voting cap materially affect who controls amendments and workouts.

nodes.label: doc-a::IX::9.04g-loan-buybacks
nodes.notes: $20,000,000 aggregate cap on non-pro-rata open market buybacks; unlimited via Dutch Auction. Debt bought back must be cancelled, so this is a deleveraging (not a sponsor-hold) construct.

nodes.label: doc-a::IX::9.08-right-of-setoff
nodes.notes: Setoff is one of only two rights a Secured Party may exercise individually notwithstanding Section 8.07.

nodes.label: doc-a::IX::9.09-governing-law-jurisdiction
nodes.notes: Illinois (not New York) governing law is unusual for a syndicated facility of this size and is a genuinely distinguishing term.

nodes.label: doc-a::IX::9.17-interest-rate-limitation
nodes.notes: Paired with the separate Canadian criminal-rate adjustment in Section 2.13(h).

nodes.label: doc-a::V::5.01-financial-reporting
nodes.notes: Clauses (c)(iii)/(c)(iv) and (j) are the mechanism by which the Restricted/Unrestricted perimeter and covenant compliance are actually reported. Late delivery deems Category 1 pricing under the Applicable Rate definition and triggers a 5-day cure Event of Default under 7.01(e)(i).

nodes.label: doc-a::V::5.02-notices-of-material-events
nodes.notes: Breach of 5.02(a) alone is an immediate Event of Default under 7.01(d) with no cure period; breaches of the other 5.02 clauses get a 5-day cure under 7.01(e)(i).

nodes.label: doc-a::V::5.03-existence-conduct
nodes.notes: Breach of 5.03 with respect to a Loan Party's EXISTENCE is an immediate Event of Default under 7.01(d) with no cure period; other 5.03 breaches get 30 days under 7.01(e)(ii).

nodes.label: doc-a::V::5.04-payment-of-obligations
nodes.notes: The contest exception is cross-referenced by Permitted Encumbrances clauses (a) and (b).

nodes.label: doc-a::V::5.06-books-records-inspection
nodes.notes: The one-inspection-per-year limit and the Event-of-Default field-exam right are real, negotiated economics; breach carries only the 5-day cure of 7.01(e)(i).

nodes.label: doc-a::V::5.08-use-of-proceeds
nodes.notes: The DDTL use-of-proceeds restriction is a hard purpose limitation. Breach of 5.08 is an immediate Event of Default under 7.01(d) with no cure period.

nodes.label: doc-a::V::5.12-casualty-condemnation
nodes.notes: Links to the Prepayment Event definition clause (a)(iii) casualty/condemnation sweep.

nodes.label: doc-a::V::5.13-additional-collateral
nodes.notes: CRITICAL entity-scope provision: determines who becomes a guarantor and what is pledged. The material-adverse-tax-consequence and cost/benefit escapes, plus the no-non-US/Canada-perfection rule, materially limit the collateral package. Breach carries only a 5-day cure under 7.01(e)(i).

nodes.label: Entity scope @ 5.13
nodes.notes: CRITICAL entity-scope provision: determines who becomes a guarantor and what is pledged. The material-adverse-tax-consequence and cost/benefit escapes, plus the no-non-US/Canada-perfection rule, materially limit the collateral package. Breach carries only a 5-day cure under 7.01(e)(i).

nodes.label: doc-a::V::5.14-post-closing
nodes.notes: FLAGGED AS UNCERTAIN: the entire operative content of this covenant lives on Schedule 5.14, which is NOT reproduced in this filed exhibit, so neither the required actions nor their deadlines can be determined from this document. The stakes are high - breach is an immediate Event of Default under Section 7.01(d) with no cure period - so materiality could be anywhere from INFORMATIONAL to CRITICAL depending on schedule content that is not available here.

nodes.label: doc-a::V::5.15-unrestricted-subsidiary-designation
nodes.notes: CRITICAL: this is the trap-door for moving assets outside the covenant perimeter; the IP restriction in clause (e) plus the 6.05 flush IP prohibition are the anti-drop-down protections.

nodes.label: doc-a::V::chapeau
nodes.notes: ENTITY SCOPE: covenants bind Loan Parties and (where stated) Restricted Subsidiaries - Unrestricted Subsidiaries are outside the covenant perimeter.

nodes.label: Entity scope @ V
nodes.notes: ENTITY SCOPE: covenants bind Loan Parties and (where stated) Restricted Subsidiaries - Unrestricted Subsidiaries are outside the covenant perimeter.

nodes.label: doc-a::VI::6.01b
nodes.notes: SHARED CAP: 6.01(b)(iii), 6.01(c)(iii) and 6.04(b) share a single 15% of Applicable EBITDA cap on U.S.-Loan-Party exposure to non-U.S.-Loan-Party Restricted Subsidiaries. Note 6.04(b)'s own text says '15% of EBITDA' rather than Applicable EBITDA - an internal drafting inconsistency.

nodes.label: doc-a::VI::6.01c
nodes.notes: Second leg of the shared 15% of Applicable EBITDA cap.

nodes.label: doc-a::VI::6.01e
nodes.notes: FLAGGED AS UNCERTAIN (entity applicability): the basket is uncapped but by its terms extends only to 'any Loan Party', whereas the Section 6.01 chapeau restricts both Loan Parties AND Restricted Subsidiaries and most sibling clauses (e.g. (l), (m), (p)) expressly cover 'the Company or any Restricted Subsidiary'. It is unclear from the text whether a non-Loan-Party Restricted Subsidiary may incur ordinary-course performance/bid/appeal/surety bond obligations at all.

nodes.label: doc-a::VI::6.01f
nodes.notes: Schedule 6.01 is not reproduced in this document, so the grandfathered amount cannot be determined from this text.

nodes.label: doc-a::VI::6.01g
nodes.notes: This is the general refinancing conduit and is also incorporated into 6.01(p) for purchase-money debt.

nodes.label: doc-a::VI::6.01h
nodes.notes: Hard $20,000,000 cap; note the clause is drafted around designation as a Restricted Subsidiary rather than acquisitions generally (6.01(m) covers Permitted Acquisition debt).

nodes.label: doc-a::VI::6.01m
nodes.notes: UNCAPPED acquisition-debt basket - capacity is governed indirectly by the Permitted Acquisition conditions (pro forma leverage 0.25x inside the covenant, liquidity test) rather than by any dollar or ratio limit here.

nodes.label: doc-a::VI::6.01o
nodes.notes: Paired with the 6.02(o) Lien basket and 6.05(j) Disposition basket.

nodes.label: doc-a::VI::6.01p
nodes.notes: Grower basket expressed solely as a percentage of Applicable EBITDA with no dollar floor; secured by the corresponding 6.02(j) Lien basket.

nodes.label: doc-a::VI::6.01q
nodes.notes: Greater-of grower basket. Note it is NOT expressly conditioned on absence of a Default.

nodes.label: doc-a::VI::6.02c
nodes.notes: Schedule 6.02 is not reproduced in this document.

nodes.label: doc-a::VI::6.02d
nodes.notes: The express exclusion of Unrestricted-to-Restricted redesignations closes a leakage path.

nodes.label: doc-a::VI::6.02j
nodes.notes: Capacity is derivative of the 6.01(p) 15% of Applicable EBITDA basket - a linked debt/Lien pair.

nodes.label: doc-a::VI::6.02p
nodes.notes: Mirrors the 6.01(q) general debt basket in size but is a SEPARATE basket - the two are not expressly linked, so obligations could in principle use 6.01(q) capacity and 6.02(p) capacity independently.

nodes.label: doc-a::VI::6.03a-mergers
nodes.notes: The survivorship rules are drafted to preserve the U.S./Canadian ring-fence - a Canadian entity may never end up as the surviving entity where a U.S. Loan Party is involved.

nodes.label: doc-a::VI::6.03d-fiscal-year
nodes.notes: Prevents manipulation of four-quarter covenant measurement periods.

nodes.label: doc-a::VI::6.03e-accounting-basis
nodes.notes: Works together with the Section 1.04 GAAP-freeze mechanic.

nodes.label: doc-a::VI::6.03g-canadian-db-plans
nodes.notes: An acquisition-blocking covenant: it can prohibit an otherwise-Permitted Acquisition of a target with Canadian DB plan history.

nodes.label: doc-a::VI::6.04-chapeau
nodes.notes: Note the covenant also restricts the mere FORMATION of new subsidiaries after the Effective Date.

nodes.label: doc-a::VI::6.04-unrestricted-sub-valuation
nodes.notes: This is the anti-J.Crew style valuation mechanic and is easy to overlook because it sits in unlettered flush text at the end of Section 6.04.

nodes.label: doc-a::VI::6.04b
nodes.notes: FLAGGED AS UNCERTAIN: this clause is unquestionably important (it is the third leg of the shared 15% cap and would otherwise be CRITICAL), but its own scope is ambiguous on the face of the text - it says '15% of EBITDA' while the parallel provisos in 6.01(b)(iii) and 6.01(c)(iii) describing the SAME shared cap say '15% of Applicable EBITDA'. 'EBITDA' and 'Applicable EBITDA' are separately defined terms with different measurement conventions, so the size of the shared cap cannot be determined with confidence from this text.

nodes.label: doc-a::VI::6.04c
nodes.notes: The 'without regard to write-downs or write-offs' language prevents rebuilding capacity by impairing intercompany loans.

nodes.label: doc-a::VI::6.04h
nodes.notes: The primary acquisition basket - unlimited in size except through the Permitted Acquisition conditions.

nodes.label: doc-a::VI::6.04k
nodes.notes: Schedule 6.04 is not reproduced in this document.

nodes.label: doc-a::VI::6.04l
nodes.notes: $5,000,000 hard cap on cash employee loans; the non-cash equity-purchase loans in (ii) are uncapped.

nodes.label: doc-a::VI::6.04n
nodes.notes: Must be read with the Section 6.05 flush prohibition on transferring material IP to Unrestricted Subsidiaries and Section 5.15(e).

nodes.label: doc-a::VI::6.04q
nodes.notes: SHARED RESOURCE: consumes the same Available Amount as Section 6.08(a)(iv) Restricted Payments, and usage under either reduces the Available Amount via clause (viii) of its definition. Requires a 0.50x leverage cushion.

nodes.label: doc-a::VI::6.04r
nodes.notes: Unlike 6.01(q) and 6.02(p), this general basket IS conditioned on no Event of Default.

nodes.label: doc-a::VI::6.05-ip-flush-prohibition
nodes.notes: Explicit anti-J.Crew blocker; overrides every other Section 6.05 exception and mirrors Section 5.15(e).

nodes.label: doc-a::VI::6.05a
nodes.notes: Uncapped and not subject to the mandatory prepayment sweep (only 6.05(k) sales are Prepayment Events).

nodes.label: doc-a::VI::6.05b
nodes.notes: Cross-border U.S./Canadian transfers between Loan Parties are policed through the affiliate-transaction covenant - a direct consequence of the ring-fence.

nodes.label: doc-a::VI::6.05f
nodes.notes: Note the Net Proceeds of such events are still Prepayment Events under clause (a)(iii) of that definition.

nodes.label: doc-a::VI::6.05i
nodes.notes: The express IP carve-out from this clause is part of the anti-IP-leakage architecture.

nodes.label: doc-a::VI::6.05k
nodes.notes: CRITICAL LINKAGE: this is the ONLY Disposition basket that triggers the Section 2.11(c) mandatory prepayment sweep (via clause (a)(i) of 'Prepayment Event'), and it is an annual (per fiscal year) basket rather than a cumulative one.

nodes.label: doc-a::VI::6.06-sale-leaseback
nodes.notes: Effectively limited to purchase-money-style sale-leasebacks within 180 days of acquisition; no separate dollar basket.

nodes.label: doc-a::VI::6.07-swap-agreements
nodes.notes: Anti-speculation covenant; only Swap Agreements with Lenders or Lender Affiliates become Swap Agreement Obligations sharing in the Collateral.

nodes.label: doc-a::VI::6.08a-i
nodes.notes: Stock-only dividends; no cash leakage.

nodes.label: doc-a::VI::6.08a-ii
nodes.notes: Ratable requirement protects the Loan Party group's proportionate share where minority holders exist.

nodes.label: doc-a::VI::6.08a-iii
nodes.notes: UNCAPPED management-equity basket with no dollar limit and no Default condition stated - unusually permissive.

nodes.label: doc-a::VI::6.08a-iv
nodes.notes: SHARED RESOURCE: draws on the same Available Amount as Section 6.04(q) investments; usage reduces the Available Amount via clause (viii) of its definition.

nodes.label: doc-a::VI::6.08a-v
nodes.notes: CRITICAL: the final proviso converts the $10,000,000 annual cap into an UNLIMITED leverage-based dividend capacity whenever leverage is 0.50x inside the covenant - a de facto unlimited-RP-at-a-ratio construct. Also note the covenant test here expressly disregards any Total Net Leverage Ratio Adjustment holiday.

nodes.label: doc-a::VI::6.08b-chapeau
nodes.notes: This is a broad restricted-debt-payment covenant reaching ALL Indebtedness, not merely subordinated or junior debt.

nodes.label: doc-a::VI::6.08b-ii
nodes.notes: Only REGULARLY SCHEDULED payments are permitted - voluntary prepayments, redemptions and open-market repurchases of other Indebtedness are prohibited unless within clauses (iii) or (iv).

nodes.label: doc-a::VI::6.08b-iv
nodes.notes: Mirrors the corresponding carve-out from the 7.01(g) cross-acceleration Event of Default.

nodes.label: doc-a::VI::6.09a
nodes.notes: Note the conjunctive test - a transaction must be BOTH ordinary course AND arm's-length; there is no fairness-opinion or board-approval alternative and no dollar de minimis.

nodes.label: doc-a::VI::6.09b
nodes.notes: CRITICAL: the intra-group exception is split along the U.S./Canadian ring-fence, so a transaction between a U.S. Loan Party and a Canadian Loan Party is NOT covered by this clause and must satisfy the arm's-length test of 6.09(a) - reinforced by 6.05(b)(ii).

nodes.label: doc-a::VI::6.09f
nodes.notes: No dollar cap on director fees or compensation arrangements.

nodes.label: doc-a::VI::6.10-chapeau
nodes.notes: Definitional hook: restrictions of the type in clauses (a) and (b) are 'Burdensome Restrictions' for purposes of the Section 3.19 representation.

nodes.label: doc-a::VI::6.10-proviso-ii
nodes.notes: Schedule 6.10 is not reproduced in this document.

nodes.label: doc-a::VI::6.12a-interest-coverage
nodes.notes: A maintenance covenant applicable to the Company (and therefore to all Lenders, not just Revolving Lenders); subject to the Section 7.03 Equity Cure.

nodes.label: doc-a::VI::6.12b-leverage-adjustment
nodes.notes: CRITICAL: an acquisition-triggered covenant holiday capped at two uses. It is expressly DISREGARDED for Section 1.06 pro forma tests (other than Permitted Acquisition conditions) and for the Section 6.08(a)(v) dividend test, but IS given effect for the Section 2.09(f) incremental facility condition and the Permitted Acquisition clause (h) tests - an inconsistency of scope well worth flagging.

nodes.label: doc-a::VI::6.12b-total-net-leverage
nodes.notes: Two hard step-downs. This level (including any Total Net Leverage Ratio Adjustment) is the reference point for the 0.25x Permitted Acquisition cushion and the 0.50x cushions in 6.04(q), 6.08(a)(iv) and 6.08(a)(v).

nodes.label: doc-a::VI::chapeau
nodes.notes: Any breach of Article VI is an immediate Event of Default under 7.01(d) with NO cure or grace period.

nodes.label: doc-a::VII::7.01b
nodes.notes: Three-Business-Day grace for non-principal payments only.

nodes.label: doc-a::VII::7.01d
nodes.notes: CRITICAL: every negative covenant breach - including every basket overage in Article VI and any financial covenant breach under 6.12 - is an immediate Event of Default with no cure period, subject only to the Section 7.03 Equity Cure for Section 6.12.

nodes.label: doc-a::VII::7.01e
nodes.notes: The five-day tier covers financial reporting, notices, inspection rights and additional-collateral obligations - unusually short for reporting covenants.

nodes.label: doc-a::VII::7.01f
nodes.notes: Threshold is $20,000,000 via the Material Indebtedness definition; extends to Swap Agreement obligations measured at net termination value.

nodes.label: doc-a::VII::7.01g
nodes.notes: This is a broad 'enables or permits' cross-acceleration - it does not require actual acceleration, so any $20M+ covenant breach elsewhere can trip this facility.

nodes.label: doc-a::VII::7.01h
nodes.notes: Triggers automatic acceleration and automatic LC cash collateralization under Section 7.02 and is the CAM Exchange Date trigger under Article XII.

nodes.label: doc-a::VII::7.01i
nodes.notes: Automatic acceleration event; also a CAM Exchange Date trigger.

nodes.label: doc-a::VII::7.01k
nodes.notes: $20,000,000 threshold with a 60-day stay period; also feeds Permitted Encumbrances clause (e).

nodes.label: doc-a::VII::7.01l
nodes.notes: Note the subjective 'in the opinion of the Required Lenders' standard.

nodes.label: doc-a::VII::7.01o
nodes.notes: FLAGGED AS UNCERTAIN: this would otherwise be CRITICAL, but the carve-out is expressed as '(other than Permitted Liens)' and 'Permitted Liens' is NOT a defined term in Section 1.01 (the defined term is 'Permitted Encumbrances'). Reading it as the narrow 'Permitted Encumbrances' list would make any priming Lien permitted by Sections 6.02(c)-(p) an immediate Event of Default; reading it as 'Liens permitted by Section 6.02' would not. The scope of this Event of Default cannot be resolved from the text.

nodes.label: doc-a::VII::7.02a-remedies
nodes.notes: Automatic acceleration applies only to bankruptcy events with respect to a BORROWER, not with respect to any Restricted Subsidiary - even though 7.01(h)/(i) are triggered by Restricted Subsidiary insolvency.

nodes.label: doc-a::VII::7.03a-equity-cure-right
nodes.notes: The cure operates as an EBITDA add-back, not a debt paydown - see 7.03(b)(iv).

nodes.label: doc-a::VII::7.03b-equity-cure-conditions
nodes.notes: CRITICAL: condition (v) means a cured quarter does NOT restore basket capacity, pricing benefit or Available Amount build - the cure is ring-fenced to the maintenance covenant only. Two-per-four-quarters and five-lifetime limits.

nodes.label: doc-a::VII::7.03c-equity-cure-standstill
nodes.notes: A true standstill: remedies are blocked from the notice of intent through the Cure Expiration Date.

nodes.label: doc-a::VIII::8.07-collateral-matters
nodes.notes: Materially restricts the rights of hedge and cash-management counterparties despite their sharing in the Collateral at tier four of the 2.18(b) waterfall.

nodes.label: doc-a::VIII::8.11-quebec-security
nodes.notes: Necessary to make a Quebec hypothec effective under the Civil Code; a structural piece of the Canadian collateral package.

nodes.label: doc-a::X::10.01b-canadian-guaranty-ringfence
nodes.notes: CRITICAL entity-applicability: the operative guarantee side of the one-way ring-fence. U.S. Loan Guarantors guarantee the entire Secured Obligations (U.S. and Canadian); Canadian Loan Guarantors guarantee only the Canadian side.

nodes.label: doc-a::X::10.08-release-of-guarantors
nodes.notes: CRITICAL: clause (b) permits guarantor release simply on falling below the 5% EBITDA/asset Material Subsidiary threshold, without Lender consent - a meaningful leakage path from the guarantee package that overrides the 9.02(b)(G) each-Lender consent requirement (which is qualified 'except as otherwise permitted herein').

nodes.label: doc-a::X::10.10-maximum-liability
nodes.notes: Directly caps the effective recourse against each guarantor - relevant to any recovery or capacity analysis.

nodes.label: doc-a::XI::11.01-appointment
nodes.notes: Because the Company receives and re-disburses all proceeds, intercompany flows must also satisfy Sections 6.01(b) and 6.04(c).

nodes.label: doc-a::XI::11.07-joint-several-liability
nodes.notes: CRITICAL entity-applicability: the borrower-side statement of the one-way ring-fence, parallel to Sections 2.01 and 10.01(b).

nodes.label: doc-a::XII::12-cam-assignments
nodes.notes: FLAGGED AS UNCERTAIN: the clause conditions post-CAM partial assignments on the parties agreeing their rights 'in the event of a redetermination of the CAM Percentages as provided in the immediately preceding paragraph', but paragraph (b) as drafted contains NO CAM Percentage redetermination mechanic (it addresses only pro rata distribution). Whether any redetermination right exists at all, and on what trigger, cannot be determined from this text.

nodes.label: doc-a::XII::12-cam-distributions
nodes.notes: Overrides the ordinary ratable-sharing rules for the covered obligations post-CAM.

nodes.label: doc-a::XII::12-cam-exchange
nodes.notes: CRITICAL: mutualizes currency and Borrower-specific credit risk among Revolving Lenders on insolvency or acceleration. Note 'Designated Obligations' covers only Revolving Loan principal/interest and commitment fees, so Term Loans, LC Exposure and Swingline Loans are outside the CAM.

nodes.label: doc-a::XII::12-schedules-exhibits
nodes.notes: The absence of the disclosure schedules means grandfathered debt, Liens, investments, restrictions, the Effective Date Unrestricted Subsidiary designations and the post-closing obligations cannot be quantified from this document alone.

nodes.label: doc-b::AMENDMENT::recitals-incremental-request
nodes.notes: Establishes which lender class consented to which change - relevant to whether the amendment was validly adopted for each change.

nodes.label: doc-b::AMENDMENT::schedule-i-omitted
nodes.notes: Content not ascertainable from the source; flagged rather than guessed. Any lender-level allocation conclusion cannot be supported by this document.

nodes.label: doc-b::AMENDMENT::sec2a-consent-increase-2-09e-cap
nodes.notes: A one-time, purpose-limited enlargement of the incremental facility cap that operates BEFORE the Section 2(b) restatement (which resets the cap to $300,000,000 measured after the Third Amendment Effective Date). Getting the sequencing wrong changes incremental capacity conclusions.

nodes.label: doc-b::AMENDMENT::sec2b-amendment-mechanic-exhibit-a
nodes.notes: This is the operative mechanic by which the entire marked-up credit agreement attached as Exhibit A becomes the operative agreement; it determines which version of every Article I-XII provision is in force from August 14, 2024.

nodes.label: doc-b::AMENDMENT::sec3b-third-amendment-incremental-term-commitments
nodes.notes: Schedule I is omitted from the filed document pursuant to Item 601(a)(5) of Regulation S-K, so lender-by-lender allocations are not ascertainable from the source text.

nodes.label: doc-b::AMENDMENT::sec5-reference-effect-reaffirmation
nodes.notes: The reaffirmation of Liens and the express no-novation statement preserve perfection and priority for the enlarged facilities; the no-waiver clause means no defaults are waived by this Amendment.

nodes.label: doc-b::AMENDMENT::signatory-lenders
nodes.notes: Flagstar Bank, N.A. and BOKF, NA appear to be the 'New Lenders' under Section 3(a) (signing only in the incremental capacity); Regions Bank, KeyBank and First Horizon signed only as consenting Existing Lenders and did not take incremental commitments.

nodes.label: doc-b::AMENDMENT::signatory-loan-parties
nodes.notes: Establishes the actual obligor/guarantor perimeter as of August 14, 2024 - broader than the Borrower list on the cover page because of the Subsidiary Guarantors added since 2022 (HIS Company, Interworld Highway, S&S Automotive).

nodes.label: doc-b::II::2-01-commitments
nodes.notes: Clause (e) is the new-money commitment created by this Amendment; the Canadian ring-fence flush language is an entity-applicability rule.

nodes.label: doc-b::II::2-06-letters-of-credit
nodes.notes: The $25,000,000 aggregate LC Exposure cap sits inside the (now $255,000,000) Revolving Commitments.

nodes.label: doc-b::II::2-09-commitments-increase-incremental
nodes.notes: Two capacity changes interact: Section 2(a) of the Amendment temporarily lifted the old cap from $200,000,000 to $255,000,000 to permit this deal, and the restated Section 2.09(e)(ii) then resets the cap to $300,000,000 measured from the Third Amendment Effective Date - so the $200,000,000 term loan and $55,000,000 revolver increase funded under this Amendment do NOT consume the reset $300,000,000 basket. Also note the MFN now protects the new tranche.

nodes.label: doc-b::II::2-10-repayment-amortization
nodes.notes: The new $2,500,000 quarterly amortization on a $200,000,000 tranche is 1.25% per quarter (5% per annum).

nodes.label: doc-b::II::2-11-prepayment-of-loans
nodes.notes: Declined Amounts feed the Available Amount builder basket, linking the prepayment waterfall to Sections 6.04(q) and 6.08(a)(iv) capacity.

nodes.label: doc-b::II::2-18-payments-allocation-sharing
nodes.notes: The Section 2.22 notice requirement is what determines whether hedge and cash-management claims share pari passu at the fourth tier or drop to the sixth tier.

nodes.label: doc-b::II::2-22-banking-services-swap-agreements
nodes.notes: The JPMorgan exemption means JPMorgan hedge/cash-management claims sit in the fourth waterfall tier without notice, unlike other providers.

nodes.label: doc-b::IV::4-01-effective-date
nodes.notes: Historical conditions; retained in the restated agreement but already satisfied. Not to be confused with the Amendment's own Section 4 conditions.

nodes.label: doc-b::IV::4-02-each-credit-event
nodes.notes: Note the restated carve-out is for First Amendment Incremental Term Loans only; the Third Amendment Incremental Term Loans were instead conditioned on Section 4 of the Third Amendment itself.

nodes.label: doc-b::IX::9-01-notices
nodes.notes: The addressing changes appear to be Third Amendment edits (the prior JPMorgan address block and named individual contacts were struck).

nodes.label: doc-b::IX::9-02-waivers-amendments
nodes.notes: The express carve-out in clause (B) - that amendments to financial covenants or their defined terms are not interest/fee reductions - is what allowed the Section 6.12 and definitional changes here to pass on a Required Lender vote.

nodes.label: doc-b::IX::9-04-successors-assigns
nodes.notes: The 20% Affiliate Lender Cap, the 25% Debt Fund Affiliate voting cap and the $20,000,000 open-market buyback limit are hard numerical constraints that interact with the Required Lenders definition.

nodes.label: doc-b::V::5-01-financial-statements
nodes.notes: Delivery of Section 5.01(a)/(b) financials is the trigger point for Applicable EBITDA, Applicable Rate changes and pro forma testing throughout the agreement.

nodes.label: doc-b::V::5-02-notices-of-material-events
nodes.notes: Breach of Section 5.02(a) is an immediate Event of Default under Section 7.01(d) with no grace period; the balance of Section 5.02 gets a five-day cure under Section 7.01(e)(i).

nodes.label: doc-b::V::5-03-existence-conduct-of-business
nodes.notes: Failure as to a Loan Party's existence is an immediate Event of Default under Section 7.01(d).

nodes.label: doc-b::V::5-06-books-records-inspection
nodes.notes: Breach carries the shorter five-day cure period under Section 7.01(e)(i).

nodes.label: doc-b::V::5-08-use-of-proceeds
nodes.notes: Breach of Section 5.08 is an immediate Event of Default under Section 7.01(d). The 'replenish cash previously used to finance Permitted Acquisitions' language expressly permits reimbursement of the Source Atlantic Acquisition funding.

nodes.label: doc-b::V::5-13-additional-collateral-further-assurances
nodes.notes: Core entity-applicability and collateral-scope provision; breach carries the five-day cure under Section 7.01(e)(i).

nodes.label: doc-b::V::5-14-post-closing-requirements
nodes.notes: Breach is an immediate Event of Default under Section 7.01(d); the underlying Schedule 5.14 is not restated in this Amendment (Schedules other than the Commitment Schedule remain as most recently delivered).

nodes.label: doc-b::V::5-15-designation-of-unrestricted-subsidiaries
nodes.notes: Designation consumes Section 6.04 investment capacity and can rebuild the Available Amount on redesignation - a shared-resource relationship.

nodes.label: doc-b::VI::6-01-b
nodes.notes: Clause (b)(iii) is a SHARED 15% of Applicable EBITDA cap across Sections 6.01(b)(iii), 6.01(c)(iii) and 6.04(b) - drawing on one reduces the others.

nodes.label: doc-b::VI::6-01-c
nodes.notes: Same shared 15% of Applicable EBITDA cap as Sections 6.01(b)(iii) and 6.04(b).

nodes.label: doc-b::VI::6-01-f
nodes.notes: Schedule 6.01 is not restated by this Amendment and remains in the form most recently delivered.

nodes.label: doc-b::VI::6-01-m
nodes.notes: Uncapped acquisition-debt basket - its size is limited only by the Permitted Acquisition conditions (including pro forma Section 6.12 compliance with a 0.25x cushion).

nodes.label: doc-b::VI::6-01-o
nodes.notes: Paired with the Lien permission in Section 6.02(o) and the Disposition permission in Section 6.05(j).

nodes.label: doc-b::VI::6-01-p
nodes.notes: Paired with the Lien permission in Section 6.02(j), which cross-references this basket.

nodes.label: doc-b::VI::6-01-q
nodes.notes: General debt basket; grows with Applicable EBITDA.

nodes.label: doc-b::VI::6-02-b
nodes.notes: Incorporates the ten-clause Permitted Encumbrances definition, which excludes Liens securing Indebtedness other than clauses (d) and (e) of that definition.

nodes.label: doc-b::VI::6-02-j
nodes.notes: Directly tied to and capped by the Section 6.01(p) 15% of Applicable EBITDA basket.

nodes.label: doc-b::VI::6-02-p
nodes.notes: General Lien basket; note it is sized identically to but is separate from the Section 6.01(q), 6.04(r) and 6.05(k) baskets.

nodes.label: doc-b::VI::6-03-a
nodes.notes: Directional survivorship rules preserve the U.S./Canadian credit split.

nodes.label: doc-b::VI::6-03-g
nodes.notes: An acquisition-blocking provision that operates independently of the Permitted Acquisition definition.

nodes.label: doc-b::VI::6-04-b
nodes.notes: Third leg of the shared 15% cap with Sections 6.01(b)(iii) and 6.01(c)(iii). Note the text of this clause references '15% of EBITDA' whereas the two Section 6.01 legs reference '15% of Applicable EBITDA' - flagging the inconsistency rather than reconciling it.

nodes.label: doc-b::VI::6-04-c
nodes.notes: Also draws on the shared 15% cap.

nodes.label: doc-b::VI::6-04-h
nodes.notes: Unlimited in amount but fully conditioned by the Permitted Acquisition definition, including its $50,000,000 term-of-agreement cap on acquisitions of non-Loan-Parties and non-Collateral assets.

nodes.label: doc-b::VI::6-04-q
nodes.notes: Draws on the same Available Amount as Restricted Payments under Section 6.08(a)(iv) and carries a 0.5x leverage cushion condition.

nodes.label: doc-b::VI::6-04-r
nodes.notes: General investment basket.

nodes.label: doc-b::VI::6-05-b
nodes.notes: Cross-border Loan Party transfers are routed through the affiliate transaction covenant.

nodes.label: doc-b::VI::6-05-e
nodes.notes: Clause (e)(ii) is a dedicated $20,000,000 HISCO asset carve-out that is also excluded from the Section 6.06 180-day timing requirement.

nodes.label: doc-b::VI::6-05-ip-to-unrestricted-sub-prohibition
nodes.notes: A cross-covenant anti-trap-door provision that overrides the Section 6.02, 6.04, 6.05 and 6.08 permissions.

nodes.label: doc-b::VI::6-05-k
nodes.notes: This is the only Disposition basket whose Net Proceeds trigger the Section 2.11(c) mandatory prepayment sweep via clause (a)(i) of the Prepayment Event definition. Note the annual (not cumulative) reset.

nodes.label: doc-b::VI::6-06-sale-leaseback
nodes.notes: The carve-out from clause (b) makes the Section 6.05(e)(ii) HISCO basket and the Section 6.05(k) general basket the routes for sale-leasebacks of seasoned assets.

nodes.label: doc-b::VI::6-08a-iv
nodes.notes: Shares the Available Amount with Section 6.04(q) investments; the hard 2.5x ceiling is more restrictive than the 0.5x-cushion test used for investments.

nodes.label: doc-b::VI::6-08a-v
nodes.notes: The dollar cap is effectively unlimited at sub-2.5x leverage; note the express disregard of any Total Net Leverage Ratio Adjustment for the pro forma test.

nodes.label: doc-b::VI::6-09-lead-in
nodes.notes: Note clause (b) permits intra-U.S. and intra-Canadian Loan Party transactions but NOT cross-border Loan Party transactions, which must instead satisfy clause (a)'s arm's-length and ordinary-course tests - the mechanism Section 6.05(b) relies on.

nodes.label: doc-b::VI::6-10-restrictive-agreements
nodes.notes: Defines 'Burdensome Restrictions' for the Section 3.19 representation.

nodes.label: doc-b::VI::6-11-amendment-of-material-documents
nodes.notes: The Source Atlantic Share Purchase Agreement was NOT added to this list even though the Source Atlantic Acquisition was added to the Permitted Acquisition definition.

nodes.label: doc-b::VI::6-12a-interest-coverage-ratio
nodes.notes: Unchanged level; tested quarterly with no step-downs and no Total Net Leverage Ratio Adjustment analogue.

nodes.label: doc-b::VI::6-12b-total-net-leverage-ratio
nodes.notes: Two Third Amendment changes here: the usage counter is reset to run from the Third Amendment Effective Date (previously the First Amendment Effective Date), and the Source Atlantic Acquisition adjustment is free of charge. Because the current level (until September 30, 2024) is already 4.50x, the 4.50x hard ceiling means no adjustment headroom exists in that window.

nodes.label: doc-b::VII::7-01-events-of-default
nodes.notes: Clause (d)'s no-grace treatment of every Article VI covenant is what makes each basket-level analysis in Article VI immediately consequential.

nodes.label: doc-b::VII::7-03-equity-cure
nodes.notes: The express exclusion of Specified Equity Contributions from the Available Amount and from pro forma basket tests prevents an equity cure from also creating covenant capacity.

nodes.label: doc-b::X::10-01-guaranty
nodes.notes: The single most important entity-applicability rule in the structure: Canadian credit support runs only to Canadian Secured Obligations.

nodes.label: doc-b::XII::12-cam
nodes.notes: Applies only to Revolving Lenders and Designated Obligations (Revolving Loan principal/interest and commitment fees), not to the Term facilities.

nodes.label: doc-c::preamble-parties-and-date
nodes.notes: Records the corporate name change (Lawson Products, Inc. -> Distribution Solutions Group, Inc.) that matters for entity-applicability analysis; note that Lawson Products, Inc. ALSO separately signs as a Borrower, so the two are distinct entities notwithstanding the 'formerly known as' parenthetical for the parent.

nodes.label: doc-c::recital-agreement-to-amend
nodes.notes: No independent operative effect.

nodes.label: doc-c::rp-condition-x-no-default
nodes.notes: Double-sided test (before AND after). Keyed to 'Default', which is broader than 'Event of Default'. This condition applies to every payment made in reliance on clause (v), including payments that escape the dollar cap under the proviso — the proviso disapplies only the dollar limitation.

nodes.label: doc-c::rp-condition-y-pro-forma-6-12-compliance
nodes.notes: Pro forma test must sweep in associated debt incurrence/assumption, not just the cash outflow. Compliance is with the Section 6.12 covenants generally (plural), not solely a leverage ratio.

nodes.label: doc-c::rp-condition-y-tnlr-adjustment-disregarded
nodes.notes: Materially tightens condition (y) relative to headline Section 6.12 compliance and is a distinct operative rule that changes ratio-test outcomes; must not be collapsed into the general 'pro forma compliance with 6.12' statement.

nodes.label: doc-c::rp-general-basket-25mm-per-fiscal-year
nodes.notes: Residual/general Restricted Payments basket. Capacity resets each fiscal year (it is a per-fiscal-year cap, not a cumulative builder or a grower basket). Available to the Company only — by its terms it does not authorize Restricted Payments by other Loan Parties under this clause.

nodes.label: doc-c::rp-proviso-uncapped-if-tnlr-test-met
nodes.notes: Effectively an unlimited (leverage-governed) Restricted Payments capacity: satisfying the leverage test removes the dollar cap entirely rather than merely enlarging it. Two-pronged 'lesser of' floor means the escape hatch tightens automatically whenever the Section 6.12 maximum is below 3.00:1.00. Conditions (x) (no Default) and (y) (pro forma 6.12 compliance without the Total Net Leverage Ratio Adjustment) continue to apply to proviso payments; only the dollar limitation is disapplied. Payments qualifying under the proviso also do not consume the $25,000,000 basket, preserving that capacity for other payments in the same fiscal year.

nodes.label: doc-c::sec-1-defined-terms-incorporation
nodes.notes: Standard incorporation-by-reference of the credit agreement's defined-term set; note it points to the Credit Agreement (as amended hereby), not the Existing Credit Agreement.

nodes.label: doc-c::sec-2-chapeau-retroactive-jan-1-2025
nodes.notes: Determines which text of Section 3.17 and Section 6.08(a)(v) governs conduct occurring in Q1 2025. Missing this would produce the wrong operative-version conclusion for any test run against January-March 2025 facts.

nodes.label: doc-c::sec-2-retroactivity-scope-uncertainty
nodes.notes: Flagged rather than resolved. The document says only that the parties 'give deemed effect' as of January 1, 2025; it contains no express retroactive waiver or cure language, and the pre-amendment text of Section 3.17 and Section 6.08(a)(v) is not reproduced anywhere in this document, so the direction and magnitude of the change cannot be determined from this document alone.

nodes.label: doc-c::sec-2a-restatement-of-3-17-first-sentence
nodes.notes: Scope point: this is a surgical first-sentence replacement, not a replacement of all of Section 3.17.

nodes.label: doc-c::sec-2b-restatement-of-6-08-a-v
nodes.notes: Scope point for basket-relationship analysis: the other Section 6.08 permissions survive independently, and clause (v) is expressly the residual basket for payments 'not otherwise permitted to be made by this Section 6.08'.

nodes.label: doc-c::sec-3-17-margin-stock-business-representation
nodes.sectionRef: Credit Agreement Section 3.17 (as restated by Section 2(a))
nodes.notes: Regulation U 'engaged principally' test. Drafted as a hybrid present representation plus a forward undertaking ('is engaged and will not engage'), so a breach can arise from future conduct as well as from facts at signing.

nodes.label: doc-c::sec-3-17-margin-stock-use-of-proceeds-limit
nodes.sectionRef: Credit Agreement Section 3.17 (as restated by Section 2(a))
nodes.notes: This is the operative permission/prohibition limb: proceeds MAY be used to buy or carry Margin Stock so long as doing so does not violate Regulation U or Regulation X. The 'in violation of' qualifier attaches grammatically to the proceeds limb only, not to the 'engaged principally' limb above. Because the pre-amendment first sentence is not reproduced, this document alone does not show whether the qualifier is newly added; but as restated it is the operative text and it drives use-of-proceeds conclusions.

nodes.label: doc-c::sec-4a-references-mean-amended-agreement
nodes.notes: Standard conforming-reference clause.

nodes.label: doc-c::sec-4b-no-diminution-and-reaffirmation-of-obligations
nodes.notes: Guarantor/obligor reaffirmation — preserves guarantee continuity across the amendment.

nodes.label: doc-c::sec-4b-no-novation
nodes.notes: Anti-novation clause protecting lien priority and continuity of the original debt.

nodes.label: doc-c::sec-4b-ratification-full-force-effect
nodes.notes: Confirms that only Sections 3.17 (first sentence) and 6.08(a)(v) are changed; everything else in the 2022 A&R Credit Agreement and prior amendments survives unchanged.

nodes.label: doc-c::sec-4b-reaffirmation-of-liens-and-filings
nodes.notes: Collateral/perfection continuity — confirms the facility remains secured and that existing UCC and equivalent filings continue to support the reaffirmed Liens.

nodes.label: doc-c::sec-4c-no-waiver-of-rights-or-provisions
nodes.notes: Non-waiver / reservation of rights. Relevant to the retroactivity question: the Amendment grants no express waiver of any pre-existing breach.

nodes.label: doc-c::sec-4d-amendment-is-a-loan-document
nodes.notes: Pulls the Amendment inside the Credit Agreement's Loan Document machinery — representations about Loan Documents, cross-default and Event of Default triggers, expense reimbursement, and the security package all extend to it.

nodes.label: doc-c::sec-5-governing-law-illinois
