nodes.label: doc-d::I::def-disqualified-qualified-stock
nodes.notes: Disqualified Stock counts as Indebtedness under clause (l); Qualified Stock issuance proceeds build the Available Amount and fund the Section 7.03 Cure Right.

nodes.label: doc-d::I::def-dutch-auction
nodes.notes: Operationalizes the Section 9.04(f) Affiliate Lender assignments and Section 9.04(g) loan buybacks.

nodes.label: doc-d::I::def-ebitda
nodes.notes: The single most load-bearing definition: EBITDA drives the Applicable Rate grid, both financial covenants in 6.12, and every 'Applicable EBITDA'-based basket. The 20% Combined Cap is the key limiter on synergy/add-back inflation.

nodes.label: doc-d::I::def-first-lien-net-leverage-ratio
nodes.notes: Sets the 3.75x incurrence test for pari passu secured ratio debt under Section 6.01(q)(i)(A).

nodes.label: doc-d::I::def-indebtedness
nodes.notes: Gates Section 6.01 in its entirety; the earn-out carve-out in clause (e) is a meaningful exclusion for acquisition-heavy issuers.

nodes.label: doc-d::I::def-interest-coverage-ratio
nodes.notes: Denominator uses 'Consolidated Interest Expense'; a separately defined and nearly identical term 'Interest Expense' is used as the EBITDA add-back. Both are defined; the near-duplication is worth flagging.

nodes.label: doc-d::I::def-limited-condition-acquisition
nodes.sectionRef: 1.01 (Limited Condition Acquisition / LCA Election / LCA Test Date)
nodes.notes: Works with Section 1.06(b), which lets the Company test ratios, baskets and conditions at signing rather than closing.

nodes.label: doc-d::I::def-loan-party-us-canadian-split
nodes.sectionRef: 1.01 (Loan Party / U.S. Loan Party / Canadian Loan Party / U.S. and Canadian Secured Obligations)
nodes.notes: Central entity-applicability rule, reinforced in Sections 2.01 (last paragraph), 5.13(b) and (e)(i), 10.01(b) and 11.07(a). Canadian credit support flows one way only.

nodes.label: doc-d::I::def-material-acquisition
nodes.notes: Gates the availability of the Total Net Leverage Ratio Adjustment (leverage covenant step-up) in Section 6.12(b).

nodes.label: doc-d::I::def-material-indebtedness
nodes.notes: Sets the trigger threshold for the cross-payment-default (7.01(f)) and cross-acceleration (7.01(g)) Events of Default, and for the Section 5.04 payment covenant.

nodes.label: doc-d::I::def-material-subsidiary
nodes.notes: Determines who must become a Loan Guarantor and grantor under Section 5.13, and therefore who is bound by Articles VI and X.

nodes.label: doc-d::I::def-ordinary-definitions-residual
nodes.notes: Grouped deliberately; enumerating each would not add analytic value.

nodes.label: doc-d::I::def-payment-in-full
nodes.notes: Defines the endpoint of the Article V and VI covenants and of the Article X guaranty.

nodes.label: doc-d::I::def-permitted-acquisition
nodes.notes: Condition (k) is a hard lifetime cap on non-Loan-Party / non-Collateral acquisition consideration. Condition (h)(ii)'s 0.25x cushion is measured against the 6.12(b) level INCLUDING any Total Net Leverage Ratio Adjustment.

nodes.label: doc-d::I::def-permitted-encumbrances
nodes.notes: Incorporated by reference into Section 6.02(b) and into Section 6.04(g) (deposits under clauses (c) and (d)).

nodes.label: doc-d::I::def-permitted-investments
nodes.notes: Also feeds the Unrestricted Cash definition and therefore the leverage-netting allowance.

nodes.label: doc-d::I::def-permitted-supply-chain-financing
nodes.notes: Supports carve-outs in Sections 6.01(o), 6.02(o) and 6.05(j) - a receivables-monetization channel outside the general disposition basket.

nodes.label: doc-d::I::def-prepayment-event
nodes.notes: Only 6.05(k) general-basket dispositions trigger mandatory prepayment - dispositions under the other 6.05 clauses do not. Clause (b) makes unpermitted debt incurrence a 100% mandatory-prepayment event (as well as a covenant breach).

nodes.label: doc-d::I::def-restricted-unrestricted-subsidiary
nodes.notes: Entity-applicability driver: Article VI covenants bind Loan Parties and Restricted Subsidiaries only; Unrestricted Subsidiaries fall outside the covenant perimeter but are subject to the 6.04(r) leakage cap.

nodes.label: doc-d::I::def-secured-net-leverage-ratio
nodes.notes: Sets the 4.00x incurrence test for junior-lien ratio debt under Section 6.01(q)(i)(B).

nodes.label: doc-d::I::def-secured-obligations-parties
nodes.notes: Cash-management and hedging exposures share the Collateral and the Article X guaranty; Section 2.22 notice determines their position in the 2.18(b) waterfall.

nodes.label: doc-d::I::def-specified-representations
nodes.notes: The 'funds certain' subset for Limited Condition Acquisition financings under Sections 2.09(f) and 6.01(q)(vii).

nodes.label: doc-d::I::def-total-indebtedness
nodes.notes: The exclusion of undrawn/drawn LC obligations and swap mark-to-market from Total Indebtedness materially affects every leverage ratio calculation.

nodes.label: doc-d::I::def-total-net-leverage-ratio
nodes.notes: Governs the 6.12(b) maintenance covenant, the Applicable Rate pricing grid, the Available Amount investment/Restricted Payment gates in 6.04(q) and 6.08(a)(iv)/(v), and Permitted Acquisition condition (h).

nodes.label: doc-d::I::def-unrestricted-cash
nodes.notes: Cash held by non-Loan-Party subsidiaries, or in accounts without a control agreement, does NOT count toward the $100,000,000 leverage-netting allowance.

nodes.label: doc-d::I::preamble-parties-and-restatement
nodes.notes: Establishes which document is operative today and that this supersedes the 2022 agreement as amended. Note there are five U.S. Borrowers and two Canadian Borrowers; the U.S./Canadian split drives the ring-fencing of obligations throughout.

nodes.label: doc-d::I::sec-1-03-terms-generally
nodes.notes: The Quebec and PPSA translation provisions are substantive for collateral enforcement in Canada, not pure boilerplate.

nodes.label: doc-d::I::sec-1-04-accounting-gaap
nodes.notes: The FAS 842 freeze keeps operating leases out of Indebtedness and therefore out of every leverage ratio - a material capacity driver.

nodes.label: doc-d::I::sec-1-06-pro-forma-and-lca
nodes.notes: Highly consequential for capacity conclusions: it fixes the measurement date for essentially every ratio-based basket in an acquisition context.

nodes.label: doc-d::I::sec-1-09-divisions
nodes.notes: Anti-divisive-merger provision; works with the Section 6.03(b) prohibition on Divisions without Administrative Agent consent.

nodes.label: doc-d::I::sec-1-11-amendment-and-restatement
nodes.notes: This is the version-control provision: it establishes that this December 18, 2025 document is the operative agreement, that the 2022 agreement is fully superseded, and that pre-existing collateral and guarantees carry forward without re-grant.

nodes.label: doc-d::II::sec-2-01-commitments
nodes.notes: The last paragraph is the operative Canadian ring-fence and is decisive for entity-applicability questions.

nodes.label: doc-d::II::sec-2-02-loans-and-borrowings
nodes.notes: Section 2.02(a) states 'The Term Loans shall amortize as set forth in Section 2.11' but the amortization schedule is actually in Section 2.10(b) - an internal cross-reference error.

nodes.label: doc-d::II::sec-2-05-swingline
nodes.notes: Swingline availability is discretionary ('may agree, but shall have no obligation') and is limited to U.S. Borrowers.

nodes.label: doc-d::II::sec-2-06-letters-of-credit
nodes.notes: The $25,000,000 aggregate LC sublimit is a hard cap on letter-of-credit capacity within the $400,000,000 revolver.

nodes.label: doc-d::II::sec-2-09-commitment-reduction-and-incremental
nodes.notes: The $500,000,000 incremental cap is a pure dollar cap with no incurrence-ratio alternative. Note Section 6.01(q)(iv) cross-references the MFN Provision as being in 'Section 2.09(l)', but 2.09 has no clause (l) - the MFN is in 2.09(g). Cross-reference defect.

nodes.label: doc-d::II::sec-2-10-repayment-and-amortization
nodes.notes: $8,750,000 per quarter on a $700,000,000 term loan equals 5% per annum amortization.

nodes.label: doc-d::II::sec-2-11-prepayments
nodes.notes: Interaction worth flagging: Declined Amounts under 2.11(g) feed clause (vii) of the Available Amount, converting rejected prepayments into investment and Restricted Payment capacity. There is no Excess Cash Flow sweep in this facility.

nodes.label: doc-d::II::sec-2-13-interest
nodes.notes: The default rate is elective (not automatic) and applies at 2% over the otherwise applicable rate.

nodes.label: doc-d::II::sec-2-18-payments-and-waterfall
nodes.notes: The waterfall is a shared-resource provision: hedge and cash-management counterparties share fourth-tier recovery with principal, but only up to the last notified amount.

nodes.label: doc-d::II::sec-2-22-banking-services-and-swaps
nodes.notes: Failure to give notice demotes those obligations from the fourth to the fifth tier of the 2.18(b) waterfall - a real recovery consequence.

nodes.label: doc-d::III::rep-3-01
nodes.notes: A Specified Representation for funds-certain purposes.

nodes.label: doc-d::III::rep-3-02
nodes.notes: A Specified Representation.

nodes.label: doc-d::III::rep-3-03
nodes.notes: Clause (b) only is a Specified Representation.

nodes.label: doc-d::III::rep-3-04
nodes.notes: The Section 3.04(a) financials are the fallback measurement base for every ratio and basket until the first post-closing delivery under Section 5.01.

nodes.label: doc-d::III::rep-3-08
nodes.notes: A Specified Representation.

nodes.label: doc-d::III::rep-3-10
nodes.notes: Pairs with the Section 6.03(g) absolute prohibition on assuming Canadian defined benefit pension liability.

nodes.label: doc-d::III::rep-3-12
nodes.notes: A Specified Representation; tested on a Loan-Parties-taken-as-a-whole basis rather than entity by entity.

nodes.label: doc-d::III::rep-3-14
nodes.notes: Schedule 3.14 is the Effective Date designation of Unrestricted Subsidiaries and therefore fixes the initial covenant perimeter; it is also incorporated by reference as Schedule 6.04 existing investments.

nodes.label: doc-d::III::rep-3-15
nodes.notes: A Specified Representation.

nodes.label: doc-d::III::rep-3-17
nodes.notes: A Specified Representation.

nodes.label: doc-d::III::rep-3-18
nodes.notes: A Specified Representation.

nodes.label: doc-d::III::rep-3-20
nodes.notes: A Specified Representation.

nodes.label: doc-d::IV::cp-4-01-chapeau
nodes.notes: The Effective Date is the operative date for the entire restatement; the definition of Effective Date points back to this Section.

nodes.label: doc-d::IV::cp-4-01-d
nodes.notes: Confirms roll-over economics: the prior facility's accrued amounts are paid at closing rather than the facility being repaid and re-drawn.

nodes.label: doc-d::IV::cp-4-01-h
nodes.notes: Partially deferred: Schedule 5.14 item 4 allows delivery of originals within ten days after the Effective Date to the extent not already delivered.

nodes.label: doc-d::IV::cp-4-01-j
nodes.notes: Deferred by Schedule 5.14 items 1 and 2 to 30 days after the Effective Date.

nodes.label: doc-d::IV::cp-4-01-l
nodes.notes: Unusually open-ended for a closing condition in a restatement; sole-discretion standard rather than reasonable satisfaction.

nodes.label: doc-d::IV::cp-4-02-b
nodes.notes: Note the condition is 'no Default' (not merely no Event of Default), so an inchoate breach blocks new borrowings.

nodes.label: doc-d::IV::cp-4-02-override
nodes.notes: Non-standard agent-discretion override of conditions precedent - functions like a protective-advance right and could change conclusions about availability during a Default.

nodes.label: doc-d::IX::9-02-b
nodes.notes: Two provisions deserve emphasis: (1) the express statement that amending the financial covenants or their component definitions is a Required Lenders matter, not a 'directly affected Lender' matter - so 6.12 levels and even the EBITDA definition can be amended by a bare majority; and (2) clause (J), an anti-lender-liability-management protection requiring pro rata participation rights before priming or subordination.

nodes.label: doc-d::IX::9-02-c
nodes.notes: The certificate-based release in clause (ii) is the practical mechanism by which asset sales and guarantor releases occur without a Lender vote.

nodes.label: doc-d::IX::9-03
nodes.notes: Note the deliberate gating of appraisal, insurance review and field exam cost reimbursement to periods when an Event of Default exists.

nodes.label: doc-d::IX::9-04-a-e
nodes.notes: The 25% concentration limit during an Event of Default is an anti-loan-to-own feature; the deemed-proportionate-voting and Section 1126(e) designation agreement for improperly acquired Disqualified Institution positions is aggressive.

nodes.label: doc-d::IX::9-04-f
nodes.notes: Directly relevant to LKCM Headwater Investments III, L.P., which the definitions identify by name. Determines who counts for voting - an entity-applicability question.

nodes.label: doc-d::IX::9-04-g
nodes.notes: Note the $20,000,000 aggregate cap applies only to open market (non-pro rata) purchases; Dutch Auction buybacks are uncapped. Purchased loans must be cancelled, so no debt can be warehoused at the Company.

nodes.label: doc-d::IX::9-08
nodes.notes: Setoff is one of only two exceptions to the Section 8.07(a) exclusive-agent-enforcement rule.

nodes.label: doc-d::IX::9-09
nodes.notes: Illinois (not New York) governing law, notwithstanding that certain definitions reference the New York UCC.

nodes.label: doc-d::IX::9-11
nodes.notes: Relevant to the Section 5.11 discrepancy between the Table of Contents ('Reserved') and the body ('Blocking Statute Carve-Out') - the body text controls.

nodes.label: doc-d::V::cov-5-01-a-annual
nodes.notes: A going-concern qualification would itself breach this covenant; delivery under 5.01(a)/(b) is the measurement trigger for Applicable EBITDA, Applicable Rate and all ratio tests.

nodes.label: doc-d::V::cov-5-01-b-quarterly
nodes.notes: Note the first required quarterly delivery is Q1 2026 even though the first financial covenant test date is December 31, 2025.

nodes.label: doc-d::V::cov-5-01-c-compliance-cert
nodes.notes: Exhibit D requires Schedule I calculation tables for both 6.12 covenants, Schedule II for the Applicable Rate category, and Schedule III listing Unrestricted Subsidiaries.

nodes.label: doc-d::V::cov-5-01-e-through-j
nodes.notes: Clause (j) is the mechanism by which Lenders can see the covenant-perimeter (Restricted Group) results separately from consolidated results.

nodes.label: doc-d::V::cov-5-02-notices
nodes.notes: Breach of 5.02(a) (Default notice) is an immediate Event of Default under Section 7.01(d) with no grace period; breach of the other clauses gets a five-day cure under 7.01(e)(i). Section 8.02(b) makes the specific heading a condition of deemed Administrative Agent knowledge.

nodes.label: doc-d::V::cov-5-03-existence
nodes.notes: Breach of 5.03 with respect to a Loan Party's existence is an immediate Event of Default under Section 7.01(d).

nodes.label: doc-d::V::cov-5-06-books-and-inspection
nodes.notes: Field examination rights are unlocked only by a continuing Event of Default; Section 9.03(a)(B) makes field exam costs reimbursable only during an Event of Default.

nodes.label: doc-d::V::cov-5-08-use-of-proceeds
nodes.notes: Breach of Section 5.08 is an immediate Event of Default under Section 7.01(d) with no grace period.

nodes.label: doc-d::V::cov-5-11-blocking-statute
nodes.notes: Materiality flagged uncertain because it partially qualifies the Sanctions covenants for Canadian entities. Also note a document defect: the Table of Contents lists Section 5.11 as 'Reserved', but the body contains this substantive Blocking Statute Carve-Out.

nodes.label: doc-d::V::cov-5-12-casualty-condemnation
nodes.notes: Ties casualty and condemnation events into the Section 2.11(c) mandatory prepayment machinery via clause (a)(iii) of Prepayment Event.

nodes.label: doc-d::V::cov-5-13-additional-collateral
nodes.notes: This section, together with the Material Subsidiary definition, determines who is bound as a guarantor/grantor. There is no express foreign-subsidiary equity pledge limitation (e.g., no 65% CFC pledge cap), but clause (e)(ii) removes any obligation to perfect outside the U.S. and Canada.

nodes.label: doc-d::V::cov-5-14-post-closing
nodes.notes: Breach of Section 5.14 is an immediate Event of Default under Section 7.01(d) with no grace period, which makes these dated deliverables unusually consequential.

nodes.label: doc-d::V::cov-5-15-unrestricted-subsidiary-designation
nodes.notes: Core anti-leakage architecture. Combined with Section 6.04(r)'s dedicated cap and the no-reallocation rule, the agreement tightly limits value transfer to Unrestricted Subsidiaries.

nodes.label: doc-d::V::cov-chapeau
nodes.notes: Entity applicability: the affirmative covenants bind Loan Parties (and, where stated, Restricted Subsidiaries), not Unrestricted Subsidiaries.

nodes.label: doc-d::VI::6-01-b
nodes.notes: SHARED BASKET: the 15% of Applicable EBITDA cap in 6.01(b)(iii) is a single aggregate cap shared with 6.01(c)(iii) and 6.04(b). Usage under any one reduces capacity under the others.

nodes.label: doc-d::VI::6-01-c
nodes.notes: SHARED BASKET with 6.01(b)(iii) and 6.04(b).

nodes.label: doc-d::VI::6-01-f
nodes.notes: Grandfathered existing debt is small; the facility itself is essentially the entire capital structure.

nodes.label: doc-d::VI::6-01-h
nodes.notes: Applies to redesignation of Unrestricted Subsidiaries as Restricted; note Section 5.15 treats redesignation as an incurrence of that Subsidiary's existing Indebtedness.

nodes.label: doc-d::VI::6-01-j
nodes.notes: Uncapped; Banking Services Obligations are also Secured Obligations sharing the Collateral and the 2.18(b) waterfall.

nodes.label: doc-d::VI::6-01-m
nodes.notes: Uncapped in dollar terms - capacity is governed indirectly by the Permitted Acquisition conditions (including pro forma compliance with Section 6.12 plus the 0.25x cushion).

nodes.label: doc-d::VI::6-01-o
nodes.notes: Uncapped in this section; pairs with the Lien exception in 6.02(o) and the Disposition exception in 6.05(j).

nodes.label: doc-d::VI::6-01-p
nodes.notes: Grows with EBITDA; corresponding Liens are permitted by Section 6.02(j). Note this 15% cap is separate from and additional to the 15% shared intercompany cap.

nodes.label: doc-d::VI::6-01-q
nodes.notes: The principal incurrence-based debt capacity. Note the incurrence levels (3.75x first lien / 4.00x secured) sit at or below the 4.25x maintenance level, and clause (ii)(A)(3) bars non-Loan-Party obligors, closing the classic structural-subordination leak. Clause (iv) cross-references 'Section 2.09(l)' for the MFN Provision, but the MFN actually appears in Section 2.09(g).

nodes.label: doc-d::VI::6-01-r
nodes.notes: The 'greater of $47,500,000 and 25% of Applicable EBITDA' formulation recurs as a separate, non-shared basket in Sections 6.01(r), 6.02(q), 6.04(s), 6.05(k) and clause (i) of the Available Amount. Each is its own basket; only the Available Amount clause (i) is shared between 6.04(q) and 6.08(a)(iv).

nodes.label: doc-d::VI::6-02-j
nodes.notes: Sized indirectly by the 15% of Applicable EBITDA cap in Section 6.01(p).

nodes.label: doc-d::VI::6-02-l
nodes.notes: The non-exclusivity requirement for IP licenses is part of the agreement's IP anti-leakage architecture.

nodes.label: doc-d::VI::6-02-p
nodes.notes: The only route to sharing or subordinating the Collateral with third-party debt; sized by the Section 6.01(q) incurrence ratios.

nodes.label: doc-d::VI::6-02-q
nodes.notes: Separate from, and stackable with, the 6.01(r) general debt basket.

nodes.label: doc-d::VI::6-03-a
nodes.notes: Note the directionality: Canadian entities may merge up into U.S. entities but the U.S. entity must survive, preserving the ring-fence and preventing U.S. assets from migrating into the Canadian silo.

nodes.label: doc-d::VI::6-03-d
nodes.notes: Prevents manipulation of the four-quarter measurement periods used in the financial covenants.

nodes.label: doc-d::VI::6-03-f
nodes.notes: Drafted as an absolute prohibition with no materiality qualifier, reasonableness standard or consent mechanism - unusually rigid and worth flagging.

nodes.label: doc-d::VI::6-03-g
nodes.notes: A structural constraint on Canadian acquisition targets; interacts with the ERISA/Canadian Pension Event default in Section 7.01(l).

nodes.label: doc-d::VI::6-04-b
nodes.notes: SHARED BASKET with 6.01(b)(iii) and 6.01(c)(iii). Drafting inconsistency worth flagging: this clause says '15% of EBITDA' while the two Section 6.01 counterparts say '15% of Applicable EBITDA'.

nodes.label: doc-d::VI::6-04-c
nodes.notes: Also consumes the shared 15% cap; the 'without regard to write-downs or write-offs' language prevents impairment from freeing capacity.

nodes.label: doc-d::VI::6-04-designation-valuation
nodes.notes: Prevents the classic trick of designating a subsidiary Unrestricted, dropping assets in, and redesignating it to reset investment capacity.

nodes.label: doc-d::VI::6-04-h
nodes.notes: The principal acquisition channel; capacity is ratio-limited rather than dollar-limited except for the non-Loan-Party $87,500,000 sub-cap.

nodes.label: doc-d::VI::6-04-j
nodes.notes: Note Section 6.05(d) cross-references 'investments permitted by clauses (g) and (j) of Section 6.04' even though clause (j) is reserved - a residual cross-reference from the prior agreement.

nodes.label: doc-d::VI::6-04-n
nodes.notes: Exclusive IP licensing is not permitted by this clause; see the 6.04 anti-leakage paragraph and Section 6.05's IP restriction.

nodes.label: doc-d::VI::6-04-q
nodes.notes: SHARED RESOURCE: draws on the same Available Amount as Restricted Payments under Section 6.08(a)(iv); clause (viii) of the Available Amount definition subtracts usage under both. Currently the leverage gate is 3.75x (4.25x less 0.50x).

nodes.label: doc-d::VI::6-04-r
nodes.notes: This is the ONLY channel for value transfer to Unrestricted Subsidiaries; the anti-leakage paragraph below makes it exclusive, non-replenishing and non-reallocable. It is a lifetime (term of the Agreement) cap, not an annual or outstanding-amount cap.

nodes.label: doc-d::VI::6-04-unrestricted-antileak
nodes.notes: Explicit anti-J.Crew / anti-trapdoor provision: it forecloses reallocation of the general investment, disposition or Restricted Payment baskets to move assets outside the credit group.

nodes.label: doc-d::VI::6-05-a
nodes.notes: Uncapped and not a Prepayment Event.

nodes.label: doc-d::VI::6-05-b
nodes.notes: The cross-silo U.S./Canadian transfer condition preserves the ring-fence by requiring arm's-length terms for cross-border asset movements.

nodes.label: doc-d::VI::6-05-d
nodes.notes: Cross-references Section 6.04(j), which is reserved.

nodes.label: doc-d::VI::6-05-e
nodes.notes: A deal-specific carve-out for HISCO real estate; unlike 6.05(k), it does not trigger a Prepayment Event.

nodes.label: doc-d::VI::6-05-f
nodes.notes: Although permitted here, casualty and condemnation events are separately a Prepayment Event under clause (a)(iii) of that definition and trigger Section 2.11(c).

nodes.label: doc-d::VI::6-05-i
nodes.notes: The express carve-out of intellectual property from this ordinary-course licensing exception is part of the IP anti-leakage design.

nodes.label: doc-d::VI::6-05-ip-antileak
nodes.notes: Second and broader IP anti-leakage lock: it reaches non-Loan-Party Restricted Subsidiaries as well as Unrestricted Subsidiaries, and applies regardless of which basket is invoked.

nodes.label: doc-d::VI::6-05-k
nodes.notes: This is the ONLY disposition clause that triggers the Section 2.11(c) mandatory prepayment (via clause (a)(i) of Prepayment Event), subject to the $20,000,000 annual Asset Sale Prepayment Trigger threshold and reinvestment rights. Note Schedule 6.05 is referenced but does not appear in the executed schedule set.

nodes.label: doc-d::VI::6-06
nodes.notes: Effectively limits sale-leasebacks to newly acquired/constructed assets unless run through the HISCO or general disposition baskets.

nodes.label: doc-d::VI::6-07
nodes.notes: Non-speculative hedging only; Swap Agreement Obligations owing to Lenders or their Affiliates are Secured Obligations sharing the Collateral and the Article X guaranty.

nodes.label: doc-d::VI::6-08-a-ii
nodes.notes: Requires ratability, so minority holders cannot be favored over the Loan Party parent.

nodes.label: doc-d::VI::6-08-a-iii
nodes.notes: Uncapped in dollar amount and not conditioned on absence of Default - unusually permissive for a management equity basket.

nodes.label: doc-d::VI::6-08-a-iv
nodes.notes: SHARED RESOURCE with Section 6.04(q): both draw on the single Available Amount and both are subtracted under clause (viii) of that definition. The RP gate is stricter than the investment gate because of the hard 2.50x ceiling.

nodes.label: doc-d::VI::6-08-a-v
nodes.notes: Effectively an unlimited RP capacity below approximately 2.50x leverage, and $50,000,000 per year above it. Note the deliberate disallowance of the covenant step-up when testing pro forma compliance.

nodes.label: doc-d::VI::6-08-b-chapeau
nodes.notes: Drafted broadly enough to capture all Indebtedness, not merely junior or subordinated debt, so any voluntary debt paydown must fit an exception.

nodes.label: doc-d::VI::6-09-a
nodes.notes: No dollar threshold and no independent-director or fairness-opinion requirement; the test is purely ordinary course plus arm's length.

nodes.label: doc-d::VI::6-09-b
nodes.notes: Note the intra-silo limitation: transactions BETWEEN a U.S. Loan Party and a Canadian Loan Party are NOT covered by this exception and must satisfy clause (a) (ordinary course and arm's length), as Section 6.05(b) confirms.

nodes.label: doc-d::VI::6-10-chapeau
nodes.notes: Anti-negative-pledge and anti-dividend-blocker covenant; also underpins the Section 3.19 representation.

nodes.label: doc-d::VI::6-10-ii
nodes.notes: With Schedule 6.10 blank, there are no grandfathered restrictive agreements as of the Effective Date.

nodes.label: doc-d::VI::6-10-vi
nodes.notes: Permits ratio debt documents to contain their own subsidiary dividend/loan blockers, judged by a borrower-determined 'not materially more restrictive' standard.

nodes.label: doc-d::VI::6-11
nodes.notes: The 'materially adverse to the Lenders' qualifier appears to modify all five clauses, though its placement after clause (e) creates some ambiguity as to clause (d).

nodes.label: doc-d::VI::6-12-a-interest-coverage
nodes.notes: Tested quarterly on a rolling four-quarter basis, first tested at December 31, 2025 (the quarter in which the Effective Date falls). Fixed level with no step-ups, step-downs or acquisition adjustment. Subject to the Section 7.03 Equity Cure.

nodes.label: doc-d::VI::6-12-b-total-net-leverage
nodes.notes: The single maintenance leverage covenant: 4.25x through the quarter ending March 31, 2027, stepping to 4.00x from the quarter ending June 30, 2027 through maturity, with up to two 0.50x acquisition holidays (so a maximum of 4.75x, or 4.50x after the step-down). Subject to the Section 7.03 Equity Cure. Several baskets test against this level with cushions: Permitted Acquisitions require 0.25x inside it; Sections 6.04(q) and 6.08(a)(iv)/(v) require 0.50x inside it (and RPs also a hard 2.50x ceiling).

nodes.label: doc-d::VI::cov-chapeau
nodes.notes: Entity applicability: Article VI binds Loan Parties and Restricted Subsidiaries. Unrestricted Subsidiaries are outside the perimeter, which is why Sections 5.15, 6.04(r) and 6.05 contain anti-leakage overlays.

nodes.label: doc-d::VII::7-01-a
nodes.notes: One of the four 'hard' defaults (7.01(a), (b), (h), (i)) used as the funds-certain carve-out standard and the trigger for unrestricted assignment rights under Section 9.04(b).

nodes.label: doc-d::VII::7-01-c
nodes.notes: Because Compliance Certificates are 'deemed made' representations, a mis-calculated covenant certificate can be an immediate Event of Default.

nodes.label: doc-d::VII::7-01-d
nodes.notes: This is the covenant-breach default. Every negative covenant breach - including the Section 6.12 financial covenants - is an immediate Event of Default subject only to the Section 7.03 Equity Cure for 6.12. Notably Section 5.14 post-closing deliverables also carry no cure period.

nodes.label: doc-d::VII::7-01-e
nodes.notes: Two-tier cure periods; note the 5-day tier catches reporting (5.01), most notices (5.02), inspection rights (5.06) and additional collateral/guarantor joinders (5.13). Cure clocks run from knowledge, not just notice.

nodes.label: doc-d::VII::7-01-f
nodes.notes: Threshold is $50,000,000 aggregate via the Material Indebtedness definition; Swap Agreement termination exposure counts toward that threshold.

nodes.label: doc-d::VII::7-01-g
nodes.notes: This is a cross-DEFAULT in substance ('enables or permits'), not merely cross-acceleration, and so is triggered by an unwaived covenant breach under any $50,000,000+ instrument even before acceleration occurs.

nodes.label: doc-d::VII::7-01-h
nodes.notes: Applies to any Restricted Subsidiary, not just Loan Parties. A 7.01(h) or (i) event with respect to any BORROWER causes automatic acceleration and Commitment termination under Section 7.02(a) and is a CAM Exchange Date under Article XII.

nodes.label: doc-d::VII::7-01-i
nodes.notes: Automatic acceleration trigger with respect to any Borrower, and a CAM Exchange Date.

nodes.label: doc-d::VII::7-01-k
nodes.notes: The $50,000,000 threshold also feeds back into the Permitted Encumbrances definition, which permits judgment Liens only for judgments that do not constitute a 7.01(k) Event of Default.

nodes.label: doc-d::VII::7-01-l
nodes.notes: Note the $50,000,000 default threshold versus the $10,000,000 notice threshold in Section 5.02(d).

nodes.label: doc-d::VII::7-01-o
nodes.notes: Interacts with Section 5.13(e)(iii), under which the Administrative Agent may unilaterally waive perfection where cost is disproportionate.

nodes.label: doc-d::VII::7-02-a-remedies
nodes.notes: Automatic acceleration is limited to insolvency of a BORROWER (not any Restricted Subsidiary), even though 7.01(h)/(i) are triggered by any Restricted Subsidiary's insolvency.

nodes.label: doc-d::VII::7-03-a-equity-cure
nodes.notes: The cure is EBITDA-additive rather than debt-reducing, and the cure window extends ten Business Days past the financial statement due date.

nodes.label: doc-d::VII::7-03-b-cure-conditions
nodes.notes: Condition (v) is important: cure equity does NOT increase Applicable EBITDA for basket sizing or improve the Applicable Rate. Condition (iv) blocks 'over-cure' by prohibiting debt paydown netting.

nodes.label: doc-d::VII::7-03-c-cure-effect
nodes.notes: This is a true standstill: it blocks acceleration and remedies for financial-covenant breach during the cure window.

nodes.label: doc-d::VIII::8-01
nodes.notes: Clause (g) is not boilerplate: it lets the Administrative Agent bind the Lenders to intercreditor terms (including junior-lien arrangements) on a five-Business-Day negative consent, complementing Sections 6.01(q) and 6.02(p).

nodes.label: doc-d::VIII::8-02
nodes.notes: The deemed-knowledge rule ties back to the specific notice heading required by Section 5.02.

nodes.label: doc-d::VIII::8-06
nodes.notes: The erroneous-payment provisions are substantive lender-side obligations rather than pure boilerplate.

nodes.label: doc-d::VIII::8-07
nodes.notes: Establishes exclusive agent enforcement and confirms that hedge/cash-management providers are passive Secured Parties.

nodes.label: doc-d::VIII::8-11
nodes.notes: Substantive Quebec collateral-perfection provision, not boilerplate, for a group with Canadian Loan Parties.

nodes.label: doc-d::X::10-01-a
nodes.notes: Scope note: the U.S. guarantee covers all Secured Obligations, which includes obligations of the Canadian Loan Parties - U.S. credit support flows down to the Canadian silo, but not vice versa.

nodes.label: doc-d::X::10-01-b
nodes.notes: The operative Canadian ring-fence at the guaranty level; reinforced in Sections 2.01, 5.13(b) and (e)(i), and 11.07(a). Decisive for any question about which entities support which obligations.

nodes.label: doc-d::X::10-08
nodes.notes: Clause (b) is a significant release valve: a guarantor whose EBITDA or asset contribution falls below the 5% Material Subsidiary threshold can be released on the Company's request without a Lender vote, subject to the anti-abuse proviso. Section 9.02(b)(G) otherwise requires all-Lender consent for guarantor releases 'except as otherwise permitted herein'.

nodes.label: doc-d::X::10-10
nodes.notes: The standard fraudulent-transfer savings clause; note the Section 3.12 solvency representation is tested on a Loan-Parties-taken-as-a-whole basis.

nodes.label: doc-d::XI::11-04
nodes.notes: Interacts with Section 5.02(a) (Default notice, breach of which is an immediate Event of Default under 7.01(d)) and Section 8.02(b) (deemed agent knowledge).

nodes.label: doc-d::XI::11-07-a
nodes.notes: Third and most explicit statement of the Canadian ring-fence, this time at the co-borrower level. Any entity-applicability analysis must reflect that Canadian Borrowers bear no U.S. obligation exposure.

nodes.label: doc-d::XII::cam-a
nodes.notes: Applies only to Revolving Lenders and only to the 'Designated Obligations' (principal of and interest on Revolving Loans plus commitment fees). Term Loans and Term Lenders are NOT part of the CAM. The mechanism mutualizes currency and multi-borrower exposure among Revolving Lenders on insolvency or acceleration.

nodes.label: doc-d::XII::cam-b
nodes.notes: Shared-resource rule: post-exchange recoveries on the revolver are distributed on CAM Percentages rather than by original exposure.

nodes.label: doc-d::XII::cam-c
nodes.notes: The provision refers to redetermination of CAM Percentages 'as provided in the immediately preceding paragraph', but paragraph (b) does not in fact contain a redetermination mechanic - an apparent residual cross-reference.
